module purpose: neorv32_cpu_counters decodes CSR accesses from ctrl_i, computes per-counter increment enables from event, halt, and debug inputs, instantiates fixed and configurable counters, stores HPM event-selection masks, and returns selected counter or configuration data on rdata_o.

use-case flows.value: CSR access qualification for counter data and HPM event-configuration registers
HPM event-selection mask written from ctrl_i.csr_wdata into hpmevent(i), with one event bit forced to 0
per-counter increment-enable state derived from ctrl_i.cnt_event, ctrl_i.cpu_debug, ctrl_i.cnt_halt, and hpmevent(i)
counter state updated by increment or CSR write, and selected low or high word formed for readback
selected fixed-counter, HPM-counter, or HPM event-configuration data returned on rdata_o
cnt_en, hpmevent, and counter storage cleared when rstn_i is low

conceptual assets.concept: CSR access-qualification decisions for counter data and HPM event-configuration registers
conceptual assets.reasoning: The start flow forms per-index access decisions with `sel(i)` and the final read/write qualifiers `cnt_we(i)`, `cnt_re(i)`, `cfg_we(i)`, and `cfg_re(i)` at lines 82-86, using the addressed CSR bank decisions at lines 90-94. Configure and read-out flows depend on these decisions: hpmevent writes occur only when `cfg_we(i) = '1'` (lines 199-200), counter instances receive `we_i`/`re_i` at lines 133-154 and 187-189, and HPM config readback depends on `cfg_re(i)` at lines 223-227 before rdata_o is driven at line 97. Integrity is established because a wrong qualification decision writes the wrong state or returns the wrong CSR-visible value; availability is established because these combinational decisions are produced whenever the address and csr_we/csr_re predicates hold, subject to the generic conditions in lines 90-94. `cnt_acc`, `cfg_acc`, and `sel` are operands of the final decisions and are therefore not listed separately.

The operate flow stores `cnt_en(0)`, `cnt_en(2)`, and `cnt_en(3..15)` from event inputs and gates at lines 108-112, after reset clears the register at lines 104-105. The fixed counters and HPM counters consume this state through their `inc_i` ports at lines 131, 150, and 185. Integrity is established because corrupting this decision state changes which counters increment; availability is established because the register is refreshed on each rising edge of clk_i when reset is inactive.

conceptual assets.concept: Base counter values for the fixed event sources connected at cnt_en(0) and cnt_en(2)
conceptual assets.reasoning: When `ZICNTR_EN` is enabled, the base counter instances at lines 124-137 and 143-156 take increment enables from `cnt_en(0)` and `cnt_en(2)`, take CSR write data from `ctrl_i.csr_wdata`, and return read data on `cycle_rd` and `instret_rd`; when disabled, their outputs are forced to zero at lines 161-166. In the shared counter implementation, `lo_q` is updated from `wdata_i` or `nxt` at lines 302-305, `hi_q` is updated from `wdata_i` or carry at lines 325-328 when `CNT_WIDTH > 32`, and the selected low or high word is returned at lines 345-349. Integrity is established because event accumulation, manual CSR writes, and CSR-visible readback must match these update rules; availability is established because implemented counter state is retained across clock edges and can be delivered on a qualified read through line 97.

conceptual assets.concept: HPM event-selection masks that choose which ctrl_i.cnt_event bits increment each HPM counter
conceptual assets.reasoning: When `ZIHPM_EN and (HPM_NUM > 0)` holds, the configure flow stores `ctrl_i.csr_wdata(11 downto 0)` into `hpmevent(i)` when `cfg_we(i) = '1'` at lines 199-200, clears the `cnt_event_tm_c` bit at line 202, and resets the register to zero at lines 196-197; when HPMs are disabled or absent, the masks are forced to zero at lines 233-237. The operate flow consumes `hpmevent(i)` in `or_reduce_f(ctrl_i.cnt_event and hpmevent(i))` at line 112, and the read-out flow returns resized mask contents through `hpm_rd` at lines 223-227 and then `rdata_o` at line 97. Integrity is established because a wrong mask changes which events are counted and what configuration is reported; availability is established because the mask is held between writes and returned on qualified readback.

conceptual assets.concept: Configurable HPM counter values for the enabled counters in the generated HPM range
conceptual assets.reasoning: When `ZIHPM_EN and (HPM_NUM > 0)` holds, each generated HPM counter instance at lines 178-190 takes `cnt_en(i)` as its increment enable and `ctrl_i.csr_wdata` as its CSR write data, while `cnt_en(i)` itself is derived from `ctrl_i.cnt_event` masked by `hpmevent(i)` and gated by debug and halt at line 112. The shared counter entity stores low-word state in `lo_q` at lines 302-305 and, when `HPM_WIDTH > 32`, high-word state in `hi_q` at lines 325-328; top-level readback ORs `hpmcnt(i)` into `hpm_rd` at lines 221-227 and then into `rdata_o` at line 97. Unimplemented HPM indices are forced to zero at lines 209-212, and all HPM outputs are zeroed when HPM support is disabled at lines 233-237. Integrity is established because selected-event accumulation, manual CSR writes, and CSR-visible readback must follow these rules; availability is established because implemented HPM counter state is retained and delivered on qualified reads.
